business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law for private and commercial matters (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991) and Common Law for federal and public law matters; legal system type is Federal_State
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA)
Canada-Hong Kong Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (FIPA)
Applicable Double Tax Agreements under Canada's network of over 90 DTAAs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC guidance for legal counsel; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (ARLPE), including beneficial ownership ('titulaires de droits') provisions in force since 1 July 2023 and Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10 (Magnitsky regime).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: The Quebec Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) receives and stores the declaration of beneficial owners ('titulaires de droits') for each limited partnership, but the personal identification data is not publicly searchable; the publicly accessible registry only states that the required declaration has been filed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing of each non-resident corporate general partner (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the partner's country of organization (e.g., Corporations Canada, provincial registry, or foreign equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention (entered into force for Canada on 11 January 2024) for documents from Contracting Parties; Consular Legalization at the competent Canadian Embassy or Consulate for non-Contracting Parties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional documents, partnership agreements, and powers of attorney of each non-resident partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry or notarial office in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French translation by a certified translator of OTTIAQ (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each individual general partner and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification in the country of origin, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; identity verification must also satisfy FINTRAC record-keeping and identification requirements for legal counsel

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, and all ultimate beneficial owners against: (1) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under FINTRAC's regime (PCMLTFA and SOR/2002-184, articles covering domestic/federal PEPs, foreign PEPs, and heads of international organizations, including persons with close or associate relationships); (2) Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Magnitsky/Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the United Nations Act; (3) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (4) OFAC SDN List, because of the business's US-dollar payment rails via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing and the US nexus of the app marketplace; and (5) publicly available adverse media and corruption databases. Screening is required at the pre-engagement stage, at filing, and on any material change in ownership or control; results must be documented and retained for at least five years under PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — registre des entreprises via the RENO online platform (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca), including the name search ('Recherche de nom'), name reservation ('Reservation de nom'), and online declaration filing modules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, the enterprise name must be in French for any enterprise operating in Quebec. A registered trademark exception allows the use of a non-French name only where the name is a registered trademark or the enterprise is commonly known by that non-French name; otherwise, a French name is mandatory. All corporate documentation, declarations, and statutory registers must be maintained in French. Transliteration of foreign names into Latin characters is accepted where phonetically equivalent and not misleading; however, the legal element of the name must appear in French or standard abbreviation: 'Societe en commandite', 'S.E.C.', 's.e.c.', 'Limited Partnership', or 'L.P.' for a Quebec-registered limited partnership.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, bank, trust, fiducie, assurance, insurance, caisse, epargne, pret ou placement (requiring prior authorization from the Autorite des marches financiers or the federal Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions)
Royal, Royale, Sovereign, Souveraine, Crown, Imperiale, Impereale, Queen, King, Prince, Princess (restricted by the Crown and public authority usage rules)

Quebec, Quebec, Canada, Canadian, Canadien, Ministere, municipal, regie, gouvernement (requiring prior ministerial authorization and evidence that the enterprise is part of or authorized by the relevant public body)

University, universite, college, cegep, ecole, hopital, hospital, clinique, medical, sante (regulated health and education terms requiring prior approval of the competent professional or educational authority)

Architect, architecte, ingenieur, engineer, avocat, lawyer, notaire, notary, comptable, accountant (professional titles restricted by the respective professional orders under the Professional Code, CQLR c C-26)
Fiduciaire, fiducie, curator, sequestre (trust and fiduciary terms requiring prior AMF or provincial authorization)
Casino, gaming, lottery, loterie, pari, game, cannabis, marijuana (regulated gaming and substance terms requiring specific licensing authority approval)
Terms implying a public authority, court, or government agency in any language, including 'Ombudsman', 'Securities Commission', 'Police', 'Army', 'Defense', 'Navy', 'Senate', 'Parliament'

Terms that are misleading, deceptive, or contrary to public order, or that suggest a different legal nature than a limited partnership (e.g., 'Corporation', 'Company', 'S.A.', 'PLC', 'LLC' without appropriate legal element)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On REQ name refusal, counsel may (1) file a revised name reservation in RENO within 15 days without additional ministerial approval if the change is only to the distinctive element; (2) submit a formal review application (demande de reexamen) with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 60 days from the date of refusal, per ARLPE sections on administrative reconsideration; (3) if the Registraire confirms the refusal, appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days of the review decision; (4) alternatively, reserve a new name with a new fee. The 180-day reservation may be renewed once for an additional 180 days by filing a renewal request and paying the renewal fee before the initial period expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional acceptance: the Quebec limited partnership must maintain a real 'etablissement' (establishment) in Quebec at a physical address that is not a mere post office box. A virtual office is accepted only where a Quebec-based registered agent (law firm, notary, or corporate services provider) offers a physical presence, maintains the statutory registers (including the beneficial ownership register), and designates a contact person available in French during ordinary business hours. A pure mail-forwarding or mail-drop address without a local service provider will be refused or challenged by the REQ and Revenu Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10-15% in the first year for a standard low-risk digital health app enterprise. The likelihood increases to approximately 20% where the declared establishment is a virtual office, the partnership has no Quebec-based employees, and the application or QST registration raises consistency questions. Unannounced inspection is most probable if the annual declaration is late, if the registered address is rejected, or if third-party complaints indicate the business is not actually operating in Quebec.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ name search and name reservation (reservation de nom) for 180 days
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff of CAD 50 per reservation application, non-refundable, indexed periodically

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the limited partnership (immatriculation de la societe en commandite) and filing of the initial declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory filing fee of approximately CAD 35 for partnerships, indexed annually; payable at the time of submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite) under Civil Code of Quebec arts. 2236-2266
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec legal counsel (Barreau du Quebec member)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: CAD 2,500 - 3,500 for a bilingual, custom-drafted limited partnership agreement including business purpose, capital accounts, distributions, governance, and dissolution clauses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register setup and declaration of owners of rights (declaration des titulaires de droits) + PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: 0.5 - 1.0 hour per entity at CAD 400 - 500 per hour, plus background screening database fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of foreign partner documents (certificates of status, passports, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in country of origin + authentication authorities (provincial authentication services in Canada or Global Affairs Canada when required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Approximately CAD 100 - 200 per document for apostille/consular certification, excluding notary fees in country of origin; market-based estimate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of English or foreign-language documents (OTTIAQ certified translator)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: CAD 0.20 - 0.30 per word or CAD 60 - 100 per page, standard 3-business-day turnaround

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and Quebec establishment address service - first year of a Quebec-based registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec law firm or licensed corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: CAD 45 - 75 per month, 12-month prepaid contract, including mail handling and statutory document service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), Articles 2209–2247 (Partnerships; Limited Partnership at Articles 2236–2247); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), sections 3, 16, 20, 31, 38 and 40
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises in Quebec) — Entreprise Québec online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are freely fixed by the limited partnership agreement, and no escrow or bank confirmation account is required by the Registrar. A foreign entity acting as general partner must be extra-provincially registered in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby consents to the formation of the limited partnership and approves the filing of the Declaration of limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the limited partnership is established at [registered office address], Province of Québec, Canada, and [representative name] is appointed as the person responsible for filing and statutory representation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all general partners and individuals authorized to bind the partnership, designated in the Declaration, be and are hereby confirmed in their capacities. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Partner be, and it is hereby, authorized to open bank accounts, execute leases, and take all ancillary measures to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and NUANS Preliminary Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Entreprise Québec portal (services.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed limited partnership name and request a NUANS name search report through Entreprise Québec. Verify distinctiveness against existing Quebec trade names, trademarks, and corporations. A favorable search permits a 120-day name reservation, after which the Declaration must be filed.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name (French or bilingual)
Description of principal business activities (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210)
Identification of all general partners
NUANS name search report request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised NUANS presentation within the reservation window or request an administrative review of the REQ refusal. Where urgent, apply for a priority name confirmation with supporting trademark evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration Data
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Barreau du Québec legal counsel or Quebec notary (private writing sufficient under the Civil Code of Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement setting out management powers, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and the rights of limited partners. Simultaneously compile the statutory particulars required for the REQ Declaration form (Form A for a société en commandite), including the identity and capacity of each general partner and the address of the registered office in Quebec.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (private or notarial writing)
Statutory declaration data (Form A)
Proof of identity of each general partner
Registered office address within Quebec
Authorization of the person responsible for filing the declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where REQ analysts identify inconsistencies, correct the Form A particulars and the partnership agreement prior to registration; an authenticated rectification by notary may be required for notarial instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Legal Publicity Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Deposit of the Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration of the limited partnership through the Entreprise Québec secure online portal. Pay the statutory filing fee (approximately CAD 52, inclusive of the annual registration fee), and collect the enterprise number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration evidencing legal publicity.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration form
Name reservation certificate (NUANS)
Proof of payment of the statutory filing fee
Declaration of a place of business in Canada
Power of attorney for service of documents if no physical place of business in Quebec is maintained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of insufficiency, supply the requested information or documents within 30 days through the online follow-up module. If registration is refused, remedy the stated defect and file a new Declaration; an administrative review is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations — QST, GST/HST Business Number, and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Joint Business Number Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with the Canada Revenue Agency for a federal Business Number (BN) and with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Identification Number (QST/QST account), GST/HST account, and income tax information return account. Where employees are anticipated, activate the payroll deduction and source deduction accounts. Use the bilingual RC59 form and the Revenu Québec online registration module LM-101-V.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (NEQ) from REQ
Limited partnership agreement
Identification of the general partner and signing officers
Banking details for remittances and refunds
Contact information for the authorized representative in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, submit the NEQ certificate and written confirmation of partnership status; request retroactive effective dates supported by the registered Declaration date. Escalation is available through the CRA Business Number contact line and Revenu Québec's business services desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Administration and Registered Office Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and Registered Agent — Internal Corporate Records Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, maintain at the registered office the register of limited partners, capital account ledgers, partnership meeting minutes, resolutions of the general partner, and copies of all filings made with the REQ. Implement an electronic records retention policy compliant with the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and calendar the annual declaration renewal obligation.
required_dossiers: First board resolution / general partner resolution minutes
Register of partners and capital contributions
Copies of the Declaration of Registration and NEQ certificate
Annual declaration renewal calendar (REQ annual update)
Electronic records retention and privacy policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is not renewed, file an updated declaration without prejudice upon demonstration of reasonable cause. Registry defects can be corrected online; late-filing fees may be waived with a documented due diligence showing current-year compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) — Digital Industries Directorate; municipal business licensing authority of the local borough if a physical office is leased
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — fitness biometric tracking and wellness telemetry app development are not listed under Quebec's industrial licensing regime; only a municipal business licence is required for a commercial office lease, and any optional professional certification under the Act respecting health and social services if clinical data services are offered

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 (clean digital services) under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23); no full EIA report or registration certificate required for office-based software development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater and zero VOC emissions for software operations; sanitary discharges limited to municipal office allowances (≤ 0.1 m³/day); e-waste and exhausted IT hardware must be directed to authorized recyclers under sections 20 and 21 of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2), with manifests retained for 5 years

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate required at the leased office under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c S-3.1) and the Quebec Building Code (CQLR c B-1.1, r. 2), including inspection of exits, alarms, and extinguishers; CNESST workplace health and safety registration for any employees, plus a prevention program and structural load clearance only if a dedicated data/server cabinet room is installed; make-workplaces accessible and verified under the CNESST attestation of eligibility for prevention and compensation coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC) — federal tax authority with Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/business/business-number.html) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); and, for the Province of Quebec, Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/) administering the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), the federal GST/HST for Quebec-based businesses, and the Quebec enterprise registration infrastructure via the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-established Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) must: (1) register the partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), which serves as the provincial master identifier; (2) apply for the federal Business Number (BN) through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or by submitting Form RC1 Request for a Business Number, indicating the partnership's general partner as the authorized representative and tax-matters partner; (3) register for GST/HST and QST with Revenu Québec once taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (the same threshold applies for both taxes), using the online Clé d'accès business services; (4) for a non-resident partnership without a Canadian physical establishment, follow the simplified CRA/Revenu Québec non-resident digital-supplier registration route, which permits electronic registration using the BN/GST program account; and (5) retain the partnership agreement, certificate of registration from REQ, and evidence of the general partner's Canadian presence or designated service address in Quebec for audit purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box entity classification election comparable to the U.S. regime. A Quebec limited partnership is recognized as a partnership under the Income Tax Act (s. 96) and the Civil Code of Québec, and its income is allocated to partners on a flow-through basis. The CRA determines entity status factually under Income Tax Folio S4-F3-C1; no domestic election is available to treat the LP as a taxable corporation. Hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act ss. 18.3–18.5 and 163.6 deny inappropriate deductions and impose filing obligations for structured hybrid-arbitrage arrangements; no additional 'hybrid mirror' election is available. A partnership must file the T5013 Partnership Information Return annually.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under the federal Excise Tax Act at 5%, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax at 9.975%, producing a combined headline rate of 14.975% on taxable supplies made in Quebec. Quebec is not a harmonized province; the QST is administered separately by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier threshold for GST/HST is determined on the taxpayer's worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated and financial supplies) for the current calendar quarter plus the preceding four calendar quarters; Revenu Québec applies the same CAD 30,000 threshold for mandatory QST registration. Non-resident digital suppliers of apps and telemetry services are subject to the same threshold with CRA/Revenu Québec simplified registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transactional clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. Electronic tax invoices are permitted if they contain the prescribed information under Excise Tax Act s. 223 (supplier name, GST/HST registration number, date, description, amount, and tax charged) and the corresponding QST rules. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework and PEPPOL network are voluntary. Taxpayers must preserve all electronic records in an auditable, readable format for CRA and Revenu Québec inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST zero-rating applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Canada (Schedule VI, Part I), (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the service is not performed in Canada and does not relate to Canadian real property or tangible personal property located in Canada, and (c) intangible personal property (including fitness-app software, source-code licences, and digital telemetry subscriptions) supplied to a non-resident where the property is not used or enjoyed in Canada. For the health-fitness app sold through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the Quebec limited partnership is the supplier; each Canadian-resident end-user transaction attracts GST/HST and QST, while transactions with non-resident end-users may qualify for zero-rating upon production of contemporaneous evidence of the recipient's non-resident status and the foreign place of supply/enjoyment. Platform commissions and payment rails do not alter the underlying GST/HST/QST characterization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration — electronic export report filed through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), successor to Form B13A, required for physical export of goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill — transportation document evidencing the physical movement of goods outside Canada for exported-goods zero-rating claims

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/foreign-exchange records — Canadian export zero-rating substantiation may be supported by bank statements, SWIFT MT103 payment confirmations, and foreign-exchange conversion records evidencing receipt of proceeds from the non-resident buyer; a formal inward remittance certificate is not a statutory Canadian requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess and claw back zero-rated treatment where supporting export documentation is absent or deficient. For GST/HST, a false-statement penalty under Excise Tax Act s. 280 applies equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax evaded, with daily compounding interest on the deficiency. Conscious evasion may result in criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment. Revenu Québec enforces parallel administrative penalties and interest for unsubstantiated QST zero-rating claims. The general partner of a limited partnership is jointly and severally liable for the partnership's GST/HST and QST remittances; a clawback therefore attaches to partnership assets and the general partner. The ordinary reassessment period is four years, but it is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) supervises AML/CTF obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible. Both current account and capital account transactions are generally free from exchange control restrictions. Profit distributions and capital repatriations to non-resident limited partners are permitted, subject to Canadian withholding tax and Quebec-specific tax reporting. No prior government authorization or central bank approval is required for remittances, provided the transaction is not subject to sanctions, tax non-compliance, or suspicious reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender regime. There is no statutory timeline or conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters and LPs may hold foreign currency in domestic or offshore operating accounts. However, repatriated funds must comply with record-keeping and verification requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and applicable FINTRAC guidance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account, Capital Contribution Clearing Account, and CAD/USD Dual-Currency Treasury Account
Operational Account and Cross-Border Settlement Account
Operational Account and Treasury Management Account
Operational Account and USD Correspondent Clearing Account
Operational Account and Payment Facility Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Nationale du Canada (in Quebec francophone markets, acting as the preferred provincial bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account, Operational Account, and Regulatory Compliance Holding Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal and regulatory viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are generally not authorized to conduct payment activities in Canada unless registered as money services businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC. A foreign EMI may provide ancillary virtual account booking services, but the Quebec LP must maintain a domestic bank account for the settlement of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds and for statutory record-keeping. Quebec's 'Act respecting the distribution of financial services and payment services' and federal Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) impose registration requirements that offshore EMIs without Canadian presence are unlikely to satisfy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Schedule I Canadian banks now accept remote video onboarding for low-risk corporate/LP structures, with enhanced digital identity verification using the director's or general partner's Canadian or recognized foreign passport. The Limited Partnership must have a registered agent in Quebec and at least one authorized signatory physically available in Quebec if the bank's internal policy requires face-to-face verification. For offshore non-resident general partners or managers, a certified certificate of good standing, notarized incumbency, and in-person or remote legal interview are typically required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner with ultimate beneficial ownership over 25% located in a FATF non-compliant jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, proof of source of funds through audited financial statements, chain-of-title documents, CIP/KYC questionnaire, independent legal opinion confirming beneficial ownership, ongoing asset declaration, and corporate registry extract evidencing bona fide LP interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital health app associated with sensitive biometric or wellness data triggering privacy and banking reputational scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Privacy impact assessment under Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, ISO 27001 / SOC 2 Type II attestation, data protection officer designation, contractual flow of data schema, and confirmation of compliance with Canada's PIPEDA and provincial health-sector rules if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border micropayments from consumer app stores without clear settlement documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commission agreements with Apple Canada / Google Canada or foreign subsidiaries, merchant of record designation, monthly settlement reports, transaction testing reports, historical ledger extracts, and declaration of the non-face-to-face sales model with associated chargeback policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of demonstrable commercial substance in Quebec for an LP claiming local operational nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full lease or sublease agreement for Quebec premises, payroll and employer remittance declarations (Relevé 1 / T4) for at least one Quebec employee, contractual service agreements, board and partner meeting minutes held in Quebec, and Quebec enterprise registrar (Registraire des entreprises) filing confirming establishment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident limited partners are routed through standard SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire messages into the LP's designated Canadian-dollar or multi-currency treasury account. The payment instruction should reference a 'Capital Contribution' purpose with no commodity code, and the receiving bank must verify the contributing entity against sanctions lists and complete an enhanced source-of-funds review. Canada does not mandate a specific FX purpose code, but the narration should cite the LP agreement clause and limited partner identification to distinguish capital injection from trade receivables, thereby lowering AML risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments and vendor settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent bank transfers, MT202 COV for interbank cover payments, and documentary letters of credit (LC) through the issuance bank when secured supplier terms are required. CAD payments to Canadian counterparties clear through Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch transactions. USD disbursements clear via CHIPS or Fedwire through the bank's US correspondent, with dual-currency accounts reducing conversion friction. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds are repatriated directly to the LP's domestic operational account as settlement deposits without additional FX intervention.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with Canadian chartered banks
Vanilla CAD/USD currency options (call/put) purchased through the treasury dealing desk
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for match-funding intercompany capital and royalty flows
FX swaps or roll-over forwards to align with monthly app-store settlement cycles
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are available only on limited bank desks but are not standard for CAD due to full convertibility; use only where a counterparty requires a synthetic offshore structure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, including UBO confirmation and principal activity update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the LP's registration date with REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration attracts prescribed late-filing charges and a default notice from REQ; failure to file for two consecutive annual cycles permits the registrar to administratively cancel the registration after notice, ending the LP's legal publicity status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips) for each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If required, five months after the fiscal year-end of the LP; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act subsection 162(7) of CAD 100 plus CAD 25 per day of default, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500; repeated or willful non-filing can lead to CRA demand action and prosecution under section 238.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit threshold applies to a private Quebec limited partnership. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under the Quebec Securities Act, carries on a federally regulated financial or insurance activity, or if the limited partnership agreement or lender covenants require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE for private enterprises. Revenue from fitness-app subscriptions and in-app purchases is recognized under IFRS 15 or ASPE Section 3400, as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: REQ requires the LP to report and annually re-confirm its ultimate beneficiaries as part of the annual declaration. An ultimate beneficiary is generally any individual holding at least 25% of the partnership interests or controlling the LP in fact. A transfer of partnership interests must be recorded in the internal register and filed with REQ as an amendment within 30 days of the transfer; the next annual declaration then re-confirms the updated UBO position. Quebec LP law governs partnership-interest transfers rather than shareholding transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited partners, with names, addresses, capital contributions and profit/loss sharing ratios)
Register of Transfers and Pledges of Partnership Interests
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions, capital call records, distribution records and general partner consent documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 140 – 500 per year for a commercial registered office or registered agent in Quebec City or Montreal
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 10,000 per year depending on app transaction volume, partner structure and audit scope; this applies if an audit is contractually or legally required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 38% federal general statutory rate (28% after federal abatement); combined Quebec/Canada headline rate for a general corporation approximately 26.6% (Quebec 11.5% + federal net 15.1%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Quebec, Canada LP is fiscally transparent; no entity-level income tax. A corporate general partner can claim the federal small business deduction on first CAD 500,000 active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%), the federal SR&ED investment tax credit (35% non-refundable/refundable rules), Quebec Innovation tax credits (up to 30%), and Quebec's deduction for qualifying intellectual property income (patent box regime).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (T5013SUM and T5013 slips) – Return of Partnership Income; filed electronically through CRA 'My Business Account' or commercial e-filing software; Quebec provincial information transmitted via Revenu Québec's 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' / EDI for Quebec tax cooperation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year Quebec partnership, T5013 return must be filed on or before the last day of the fifth month after fiscal year-end (May 31); T5013 partner slips must be issued by the last day of February following the calendar year; Quebec schedule must be filed no later than six months after fiscal period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income and partnership revenue from all Canadian and non-resident sources attributable to the Canadian operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident LP partners must ensure only Canadian-source subscription, IAP, and biometric telemetry revenue allocated to the Canadian permanent establishment is reported; do not include foreign-source digital revenue unless allocable under the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, cost of sales, and app development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred for the Canadian PE / business; intercompany charges for IP royalties and headquarters costs must comply with Canadian transfer pricing and be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification table: name, business number, residency status, and percentage allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, enter the partner's country of residence, treaty country code, Canadian individual tax number (ITN) or non-resident registration number, and percentage profit-sharing interest. Attach Form NR301/NR302 if treaty relief is sought on Canadian-source amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of income or loss for each period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Schedule 1 allocation for each non-resident partner; the partnership itself does not withhold on ordinary business allocations unless a treaty-protected payment is separately characterized (e.g., royalty/interest deemed to be paid to a non-resident).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains / losses and segregated classes of Canadian investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where gains derive from dispositions of taxable Canadian property (e.g., Canadian business assets), include in T5013 and complete the required T206 certificate if a non-resident partner wishes to pay tax remittance on gain; treaty benefits such as Article XIII Canada-US exemptions must be invoked by the partner on their own return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA: late filing penalty for a partnership return is 5% of any balance of tax payable plus 1% per month up to 12 months; false omissions attract gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax; failure to issue T5013 slips attracts CAD 25 per day per slip (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500). Revenu Québec imposes additional administrative penalties for unreported or late partnership information (CAD 100/day per file) and suspension of registrations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: General non-resident withholding tax (Part XIII) is 25% for dividends paid by a Canadian corporation; because the LP is fiscally transparent, no Canadian withholding tax applies to profit allocations qua allocations to partners, but a beneficiary is taxable on Canadian-source income through the partner's own Canadian non-resident filing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners must file Form NR301 (Reduction of Non-Resident Tax Withholding) or Form NR302 for continuous obligations, submit a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the partner's fiscal authority, and, where relevant, apply under the Canada-US or Canada-Province/Other DTA's mutual agreement procedure. The CRA or Revenu Québec may issue a Form T206 or NR301 approval reducing withholding to 0–15% depending on income type and treaty article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest (with the arm's-length interest exemption under paragraph 212(1)(b)(vii)); under applicable DTAs, royalties are commonly reduced to 0–10% and interest to 0% for arm's-length lenders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 5 million aggregate fair-market value of cross-border transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents triggers mandatory contemporaneous T2025/RC-4751 TP documentation (Local/Master File equivalent); consolidated group revenue exceeding CAD 750 million triggers Country-by-Country Report filing and notification obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Quebec/Canada does not operate an 'ESR' code in the Gulf style; however, substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule (section 245 ITA), the 'active business' requirement for FAPI exceptions, and BEPS anti-abuse treaty provisions. The LP must demonstrate real premises, operating employees, bank accounts, decision-making authority, and commercial risk for its fitness app operations to avoid sham/GAAR recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Criminal Fraud (Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Canadian-source app subscription or IAP revenue, backdating partnership documents, creating false invoices for Canadian fees, or making false DTA representations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution carries a fine of 50% to 200% of taxes evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment; civil penalties: gross negligence penalty equal to 50% of any understated tax plus daily late-filing penalties; Quebec administrative penalties may add another 20%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of a corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for source withholding, GST/QST remittances, and penalties if they directed or acquiesced in the omission; courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or maintaining the Quebec LP solely to hold the fitness app's IP or payment accounts with no real staff, no office, no Canadian bank account, or no substantive business functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply GAAR to cancel tax benefits, reassess all Canadian-source income to the partner, and impose a 50% penalty for false statements; Registraire des entreprises du Québec may dissolve the LP for non-compliance, and all limited-partner limited-liability protections are retroactively lost.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and its directors become personally liable for all partnership obligations; in a sham, limited partners can be treated as exercising control and lose the statutory limited-liability shield, exposing them to tort and tax claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Non-Arm's-Length Mispricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-resident related parties above-market royalties for IP or development services without contemporaneous Local File/Master File, or executing cross-border transactions in excess of CAD 5 million without TP documentation or economic benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess income under subsection 247(2) using arm's-length pricing; a 10% penalty is applied to the net transfer pricing adjustment where documentation thresholds are met; continued failure to provide documentation can trigger a daily penalty of CAD 100 per month up to CAD 25,000 and, for CbC reporting failure, CAD 2,000/day for corporations and CAD 1,000/day for directors/officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allowed the mispricing or who signed false CRA filings face personal penalty exposure under Quebec's director liability regime; criminal sanctions include fraud convictions and quarantine from serving as officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership and FINTRAC Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and verify non-resident limited partners or using the LP account to receive/aggregate digital payment flows (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing) without monitoring for virtual currency transfers, structuring, or high-risk PEP/non-resident transactions when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, an administrative monetary penalty up to CAD 500,000 per violation may be imposed; Quebec civil forfeiture provisions allow seizure of the LP's assets where proceeds are linked to unlawful activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are personally liable for FINTRAC violations if they instructed, authorized, or tolerated the failure; criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years and prohibition from holding commercial registrations.
